summary.name: Function as a service
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing Function as a Service (FaaS), a subset of serverless computing, along with its anti-patterns and portability issues.
use_cases: understanding what function as a service is
evaluating vendor lock-in risks for serverless workloads
summary.what_it_does: The page defines Function as a Service as a platform-level cloud capability, citing ISO/IEC 22123-2, for building and managing microservices with low initial investment. It places FaaS as a subset of serverless computing. It describes the "Grain of Sand" anti-pattern (excessively small functions) and "Lambda Pinball" (functions invoking each other in fragmented chains), which can lead to a distributed monolith. It discusses mitigation through clear domain boundaries separating public interfaces from published interfaces, and a "functionless" approach favoring native service integrations. It also notes portability issues from vendor lock-in and suggests hexagonal architecture as a mitigation.
notable: Defines FaaS per ISO/IEC 22123-2 as a platform-level cloud capability
Describes Grain of Sand and Lambda Pinball anti-patterns
Covers public vs published interface distinction for function boundaries
Discusses vendor lock-in and hexagonal architecture for portability
caveats: The article is flagged as possibly unbalanced towards certain viewpoints (January 2025)
Describes a concept, not a single downloadable tool or product
Notes the functionless approach has a steeper learning curve and integration limits vary by vendor
